study_type_evidence.quote: Finally, we tested a panel of the optimised peptides for stability in human plasma and determined in vivo pharmacokinetic parameters in rats.
Stability of selected peptides upon incubation with human plasma at 37 °C.
BLI binding Kd values and radiolabelled [125I]-GIP displacement IC50 data for purified peptides.

in_vivo_species.quote: In vivo plasma exposure levels of selected peptides upon i.v. dosing to rats.

ex_vivo_detail: Human plasma stability at 37 C over 5 h; parent B_1275 t1/2 3.5 h, linear variants ~2 h, native GIP and GLP-1 ~35-45 min.
in_vitro_detail: BLI affinity to hGIP-R ECD and [125I]-GIP displacement.

bioanalytical_quote: In vivo plasma exposure levels of selected peptides upon i.v. dosing to rats.
notes: Three of five PEPlife2 values agree with the body: 585 min = 9.75 h vs the body's 9.8 h for B_3.1; 643 min = 10.72 h vs 10.7 h for B_1275.1; 250 min = 4.17 h vs 4.2 h for B_1275.6. The other two do NOT match the body: PEPlife2 gives 3.767 min for B_1275.4 where the body says 3.5 min, and 2.367 min for B_1275.5 where the body says 1.8 min (a 31% difference). The precise values are presumably in Table S2 of the ESI, which is not in the PMC deposit, so the disagreement cannot be resolved from the body and neither value is auto-applied. Both are sub-5-minute half-lives, so the absolute discrepancy is small. The body reports no dose, no strain and no sex for the rat study; n refers to three independent experiments, not three animals. For scale the authors note semaglutide has a rat t1/2 of 7 h, below B_3.1 and B_1275.1 here.
